rawIntent: Implement Harness Universal Reconciliation v1 from the owner-authorized artifacts under .agent/plans/harness-universal-reconciliation-v1 without losing requirements, weakening proof, or performing unapproved Git closeout.
objective: Deliver a portable prompt-first plan execution system with typed closed-loop reconciliation, conversational pair repair, complete skill/provider/host parity, semantic workflow convergence, pragmatic claim verification, visible local app behavior, bounded CI, dogfood, owner-gated closeout, and Control Plane eligibility only as the final phase.

requirements.statement: A portable hash-bound resumable execution bundle preserves the full approved plan.

Ordinary conversation is a sufficient first-class entrypoint, and conversation, optional slash commands, CLI/API calls, and native host actions compile into the same canonical WorkRequest; /goal is optional and never authoritative.
Worker recipes enforce intent receipts, ownership, checkpoints, amendments, and bounded repair.
Mechanical reconciliation covers plan, implementation, evidence, providers, hosts, and runtime state.
Every registered host adapter is supported and unknown hosts fail as UNSUPPORTED.
Installed hosts receive complete selected-skill and provider parity with repair receipts.
External sources are immutable, provenance-bound, qualified, and rollback-capable.
Selected skills materialize completely across installed hosts while unselected candidates remain links.
All named provider classes have claim-specific adapters and bounded lifecycle proof.
Verification is claim-complete, pragmatic, and behavior-oriented where appropriate.
Local browser, mobile, and Pencil sessions are foreground-observable.
Pencil discovery rejects persisted ephemeral mounts and follows safe install fallback.
Routing uses deterministic facts, impact, claim class, availability, and risk.
Context concepts have one canonical owner and proven behavior remains until parity.
CI processes and waits are bounded and unavailable native runners cannot block required checks forever.
The phase dogfoods its own bundles, reconciliation, routing, and evidence.
Plan compaction preserves authority and terminal evidence while reducing active artifacts.
Closeout is exact-receipt owner-gated and leaves final main/runtime/CI state reconciled.
Typed closed-loop sensors, evidence freshness and independence, failure-to-eval feedback, expiring model workarounds, and runtime clamps mechanically bound convergence.
High-impact rules and skills are semantically converged while full-catalog structural fixtures remain green.

Control Plane remains ineligible until complete skill/provider/tool/MCP/rule/command/host/runtime parity, terminal harness proof, green exact-SHA CI, fresh installed-host receipts, and owner-approved closeout; it then becomes the final phase.

Ordinary review prompts support typed pair repair with raw-finding preservation, classification, claim-impact analysis, selective reopen, fresh evidence epochs, bounded repair packets, and immutable historical PASS evidence.

claims.statement: A portable hash-bound resumable execution bundle preserves the full approved plan.
Ordinary conversation and every available optional host entrypoint compile into semantically equivalent WorkRequests; /goal absence does not affect readiness or completion.
Worker recipes enforce intent receipts, ownership, checkpoints, amendments, and bounded repair.
Mechanical reconciliation covers plan, implementation, evidence, providers, hosts, and runtime state.
Every registered host adapter is supported and unknown hosts fail as UNSUPPORTED.
Installed hosts receive complete selected-skill and provider parity with repair receipts.
External sources are immutable, provenance-bound, qualified, and rollback-capable.
Selected skills materialize completely across installed hosts while unselected candidates remain links.
All named provider classes have claim-specific adapters and bounded lifecycle proof.
Verification is claim-complete, pragmatic, and behavior-oriented where appropriate.
Local browser, mobile, and Pencil sessions are foreground-observable.
Pencil discovery rejects persisted ephemeral mounts and follows safe install fallback.
Routing uses deterministic facts, impact, claim class, availability, and risk.
Context concepts have one canonical owner and proven behavior remains until parity.
CI processes and waits are bounded and unavailable native runners cannot block required checks forever.
The phase dogfoods its own bundles, reconciliation, routing, and evidence.
Plan compaction preserves authority and terminal evidence while reducing active artifacts.
Closeout is exact-receipt owner-gated and leaves final main/runtime/CI state reconciled.
Typed feedforward and feedback sensors, runtime clamps, failure-to-eval conversion, and workaround retirement produce a mechanically auditable convergence loop.
The high-impact workflow graph has no unresolved semantic contradictions and full-catalog structural fixtures still pass.
The Control Plane final-phase gate denies all early activation and emits the successor only after complete harness parity, proof, installation, CI, and closeout.
A normal review prompt can classify and repair a finding by selectively reopening affected claims with fresh proof while preserving unaffected terminal claims and historical PASS evidence.

tasks.goal: Unify the canonical plan/support-pack contract and compile ordinary conversation, optional slash commands, CLI/API calls, and native host actions into the same WorkRequest.
context: Existing support-pack compiler is deterministic but library-only.
Ordinary conversation must be sufficient on every host and bind to durable artifact authority.
Slash commands and native host actions are optional ergonomic adapters over the same WorkRequest.
Current pointer stays on completed V3.1 until S8 activation.
microsteps: Align v1 readers and define the new portable contract without breaking legacy artifacts.
Connect intent, plan, support-pack, checkpoints, and selective regeneration to the canonical WorkRequest ingestion path.
Compile normal prompts, optional slash commands, CLI/API requests, and native host actions into semantically equivalent WorkRequests while recording adapter identity.
Preserve optional OpenCode /goal as an emulated convenience and add no-command, invalid coverage, unresolved decision, scope, resume, and portability fixtures.
invariants: Raw intent and owner decisions remain immutable source authority.
Workers cannot author PASS or mutate before an intent receipt.
Legacy readers remain until behavioral parity is proven.
edgeCases: Material ambiguity remains at compile time.
An optional host adapter is absent or unavailable.
An amendment changes only one recipe.
rollback: Keep v1 readers active.
Disable an optional adapter without deleting compiled artifacts or breaking ordinary prompts.
failurePlaybook: Fix contract drift before downstream work.
If an optional adapter is unavailable, retain prompt-first execution and record the adapter state honestly.
stopIf: A required owner decision is missing.
The implementation would hand-edit .agent/current.json.

tasks.goal: Implement immutable external source governance and complete selected-skill parity.
context: SKILL.md is the portable source and ROUTE.json owns harness routing.
No-skill is a valid qualification result.
Selected skills must be complete on every detected host.
microsteps: Define immutable source lock and qualification receipts for skills/tools/MCP/apps.
Implement hard gates and weighted qualification against no-skill/local composition.
Project the selected set to every detected host and compare hashes.
Reject unpinned, unsafe, unlicensed, conflicting, or negative-value candidates.
invariants: Unselected candidates are never materialized.
External source content never becomes always-loaded merely because it is available.
edgeCases: A repository moves its default branch.
One host ignores optional skill metadata.
A selected skill conflicts with a local canonical skill.
rollback: Downgrade new candidates to catalog-only.
Restore the previous selected-set manifest from its receipt.
failurePlaybook: Quarantine a failed source lock.
Report host-specific projection drift without weakening other host receipts.
stopIf: A license or immutable revision cannot be established.
Qualification requires owner business preference not in the contract.

tasks.goal: Implement provider-neutral adapters for the named verification capabilities.
context: Providers are replaceable capability edges, not kernel authority.
All providers are implemented in this phase but activated only by applicable facts and claims.
microsteps: Define lifecycle adapters for Testcontainers, Pact, Schemathesis, Storybook, Maestro, Semgrep/CodeQL, k6, and OpenTelemetry.
Bind each provider to effects, prerequisites, health, timeout, rollback, evidence, and host support.
Add one positive, important negative, and unavailable/recovery fixture per provider.
Keep existing browser/search providers compatible.
invariants: A missing optional provider cannot become PASS.
Performance checks require explicit thresholds.
Telemetry evidence cannot replace product acceptance.
edgeCases: Docker or a device is unavailable.
A schema/provider is present but no applicable claim exists.
A provider process times out and leaves children.
rollback: Disable new provider IDs.
Retain prior provider registry and verification profiles.
failurePlaybook: Return explicit unavailable evidence.
Terminate timed-out child processes and retain bounded logs.
stopIf: Installation requires uncontrolled production credentials.
A provider cannot be made reversible or bounded.

tasks.goal: Implement seven-host inventory, projection, parity, and transactional repair.
context: Current runtime verification covers only four hosts while contracts list seven.
Desktop apps may be installed without a PATH binary.
A stale config directory is not an installed host.
microsteps: Introduce the common HostAdapter detect/inventory/project/probe/repair/rollback contract.
Implement fixture projections for all seven registered hosts and explicit unknown-host rejection.
Compute desired versus actual selected skills/providers/runtime state.
Repair safe drift transactionally and emit per-host receipts.
Verify live installed-only inventory without mutating absent hosts.
invariants: Unknown hosts are UNSUPPORTED.
Availability never grants task authority.
Repair never overwrites unmanaged user configuration blindly.
edgeCases: Desktop process exists without CLI binary.
A host has stale harness receipts but no application.
Repair fails after backup but before swap.
rollback: Restore every host from its transaction receipt.
Keep new inventory in report-only mode if repair parity fails.
failurePlaybook: Mark only the affected host PARTIAL.
Do not count stale config as an application.
stopIf: A host root cannot be resolved safely.
Repair would modify an unmanaged credential or destructive external state.

tasks.goal: Complete visible browser/mobile/Pencil behavior using the proven detached candidate.
context: Detached candidate d23b12a/b5231f7 passes focused build and tests.
Its advertised host set exceeds actual materialization coverage.
Live Pencil AppImage paths are ephemeral.
microsteps: Diff and migrate proven candidate behavior without blind cherry-pick.
Complete Pencil and foreground projection across all registered host adapters.
Discover stable/live Pencil launch data and reject persisted temporary mounts.
Require foreground local app observation and explicit CI headless receipts.
Implement safe user-space install and official-link fallback.
invariants: Pencil remains explicit task capability.
Design evidence never replaces browser/runtime acceptance.
Local visible-app claims need observed foreground evidence.
edgeCases: Pencil AppImage remounts under a new path.
Pencil is open but MCP is disconnected.
The environment has no display or requires elevation.
rollback: Restore manual explicit-only Pencil provider.
Retain foreground browser policy independently.
failurePlaybook: Open the official install link and return NEEDS_USER for manual GUI/elevation.
Record MCP unavailable separately from app installed.
stopIf: No visible display exists for a required local acceptance claim.
The only discovered command is an expired temporary mount.

tasks.goal: Implement typed closed-loop routing, evidence sensing, convergence clamps, and cheapest-sufficient claim verification.
context: Legacy routing still contains phrase-based skill and capability inference.
Decision Fabric facts exist but shadow mode retains legacy routing.
Existing evidence metadata does not type direction, oracle, freshness, independence, or workaround retirement.
The owner wants complete but pragmatic behavior proof.
microsteps: Route from RepoFacts, ChangeFacts, TaskFacts, impact, claim class, provider health, and risk.
Type feedforward/feedback sensors with oracle class, lifecycle timing, applicability, cost, independence, freshness, confidence, and escalation.
Add testability audit, deterministic fallback/denial states, runtime authority/delegation/proof clamps, and two-attempt repair.
Convert repeated classified failures into reviewed eval candidates and require model workaround owner, trigger, expiry, revalidation, and retirement evidence.
Select real browser/device interaction for applicable business flows and scripts for contracts.
Add seeded route precision, unnecessary activation, failure-to-eval, stale/correlated evidence, workaround retirement, and bounded repair cases.
invariants: Prompt keywords alone cannot activate a heavy provider.
Build-only proof cannot establish runtime behavior.
A worker cannot weaken verification after a failure.
edgeCases: Several providers can prove the same claim.
A cheap provider is present but lacks required capability.
Two repair attempts fail.
rollback: Return Decision Fabric to shadow selection.
Retain emitted facts and route diagnostics.
failurePlaybook: Escalate one logical capability class when allowed.
Return explicit blocker instead of silent fallback.
stopIf: A required capability has no trusted provider.
Routing would infer business requirements from a reference implementation.

tasks.goal: Converge lifecycle compaction and bounded CI.
context: Current verify-all hard-codes completed V3/V3.1 closures.
Lifecycle cleanup only purges .agent/tmp while preserving other history uncompressed.
Self-hosted certification can wait in the GitHub queue outside job timeout.
microsteps: Replace phase-specific active gates with generic pointer-driven validation while preserving historical checks.
Implement evidence-preserving content-addressed compaction and round-trip verification.
Add per-step/process/wait timeouts and detach unavailable self-hosted certification from required checks.
invariants: Raw owner evidence never becomes always-loaded rules.
Historical terminal proof is never deleted.
Required CI cannot depend on an unavailable runner queue.
edgeCases: An archive is interrupted before tombstone creation.
A historical validator is still referenced by documentation.
A CI service starts but wait-on never succeeds.
rollback: Keep compaction in dry-run mode.
Restore phase validators as compatibility checks without making them current authority.
failurePlaybook: Recover archives from content hashes and tombstones.
Fail CI timeout audit with the exact unbounded step.
stopIf: Compaction would remove evidence needed for PASS.
A context change creates unresolved canonical/mirror ownership.

tasks.goal: Converge the high-impact rule and skill graph semantically across lifecycle, planning, completion, context, delegation, research, QA, quality, and UI precedence.
context: Current structural validators pass despite known cross-file semantic contradictions.
Repository invariants cap workers at two with no recursion regardless of skill-local defaults.
Control Plane visual precedence belongs to its approved brief; generic UI advice is subordinate.
Full-catalog validation remains required after focused high-impact convergence.
microsteps: Encode the known contradiction corpus before changing policy owners.
Resolve delegation receipt shape, context work sizing, repository worker clamps, browser support loading, legacy PAF references, and Control Plane UI precedence.
Declare one canonical owner and explicit precedence for each corrected concept without duplicating prose across layers.
Run focused semantic fixtures plus full rule, skill-catalog, route, link, and mirror validation.
invariants: Runtime clamps override skill-local widening.
No prompt keyword alone activates capability or authority.
Proven legacy behavior remains until behavioral/eval parity.
edgeCases: A standalone skill advertises more workers than the repository permits.
A browser task needs QA reasoning but not the full QA skill.
Generic frontend guidance conflicts with an approved Control Plane brief.
rollback: Revert only semantic changes that fail the contradiction corpus.
Retain audit evidence and structural validators.
failurePlaybook: Report the exact owner/precedence conflict instead of merging contradictory rules.
Keep unresolved policy fail-closed and local to the affected workflow.
stopIf: Resolving a contradiction requires a new owner business preference.
A change would widen authority or weaken proof.

tasks.goal: Implement prompt-first conversational pair repair with finding classification, claim-impact analysis, selective reopen, bounded repair packets, and fresh evidence epochs.
context: Long-plan execution state lives in artifacts rather than a specific chat session.
Owner review findings may arrive through ordinary conversation during execution or after apparent PASS.
Historical evidence is append-only; only affected claims become non-terminal for a new candidate epoch.
microsteps: Define repair finding, classification, candidate epoch, impact set, stale-evidence, and repair-packet contracts.
Bind raw review text to the exact plan, repository state, candidate, and observed surface before mutation.
Classify defects, requirement changes, evidence defects, environment/provider issues, and unrelated observations with fail-closed ambiguity handling.
Compute requirement, claim, task, file, provider, and evidence impact; reopen only affected claims and preserve historical PASS records.
Generate the smallest bounded repair packet, resume through ordinary conversation, and require claim-matched fresh proof plus risk-triggered regression.
invariants: Prompt wording alone cannot choose plan authority or impact scope.
Unaffected accepted claims remain terminal.
A changed owner requirement becomes an amendment, not a disguised defect.
Historical PASS evidence is never rewritten or deleted.
edgeCases: Several active plans could own the same finding.
A finding is reproducible only on an unavailable provider or device.
A small defect changes a shared contract and expands regression impact.
The owner finding actually changes approved intent.
rollback: Disable pair-repair mutations while retaining report-only classification and impact analysis.
Restore the prior candidate epoch from append-only ledger and evidence records.
failurePlaybook: Return NEEDS_USER when plan authority or changed owner intent cannot be determined.
Return BLOCKED/PARTIAL with exact missing provider or evidence facts after bounded attempts.
stopIf: Repair would silently widen scope or alter an approved requirement.
Impact cannot be bounded from repository, ledger, diff, candidate, and evidence facts.
Repair would rewrite historical PASS evidence.

tasks.goal: Integrate, CAS-activate, dogfood, reinstall detected hosts, prepare closeout, and emit Control Plane V2 only after its final-phase eligibility gate passes.
context: Current pointer generation is 6 and points to completed V3.1.
Git closeout mutations require an exact approved receipt.
Final main and candidate SHAs both require hosted CI evidence.
Ordinary prompts are the primary portable entrypoint and optional adapters must produce semantic-parity receipts.
S7B provides conversational pair repair with selective claim reopening and fresh evidence epochs.

Control Plane V2 is the final phase and remains ineligible until complete skill/provider/tool/MCP/rule/command/host/runtime parity, terminal proof, required CI, fresh install receipts, and owner-approved harness closeout.
microsteps: Integrate shared registries and resolve all cross-slice contract drift.
Run full local verification and dogfood ordinary-prompt start, resume, review, and pair-repair paths.
Prove optional slash/CLI/native adapters compile to the same WorkRequest semantics and that adapter absence does not fail readiness.
Create the planned canonical ledger and CAS-supersede current authority after generic gates pass.
Reinstall and reconcile every detected host against the exact candidate.
Compile evidence, CI expectations, branch/worktree targets, and runtime receipts into CloseoutReceipt.
Run the negative Control Plane final-gate fixture, prove every prerequisite against exact candidate receipts, and emit the final successor handoff only after owner-approved closeout.
Stop for owner approval before any authorized Git closeout mutation.
invariants: Current pointer is never hand-edited.
Only verifier evidence can produce PASS.
No commit, push, main update, branch deletion, worktree removal, or deploy occurs before receipt approval.
Control Plane design, source edits, Docker packaging, and activation are denied before the final-phase gate passes.
edgeCases: Remote main changes after receipt preparation.
Candidate CI passes but final main CI fails.
A detected host becomes unavailable during reinstall.
Every implementation claim passes but one detected host has stale skill or runtime receipts.
An optional slash command is unavailable while ordinary-prompt execution remains healthy.
rollback: Use runtime transaction receipts.
Invalidate stale CloseoutReceipt and prepare a new one.
Use a new owner-approved supersession rather than rewriting current authority.
failurePlaybook: Repair integration failures within claim budgets.
Return PARTIAL/BLOCKED with exact CI, host, or authority evidence.
stopIf: Any acceptance claim lacks evidence.
Owner approval for exact closeout actions is absent.
Remote or local target identity differs from the approved receipt.
Any Control Plane final-phase prerequisite is missing or stale.
